description: One file per unexpected behaviour; each is pinned to the check that must fire.

files.why: Z.of_string accepts a sign and a 0x prefix: a negative natural literal would reach the arithmetic. Literals are digits only.
an object with a repeated key is read differently by different tools; refused instead of picking one reading.
a negative de Bruijn index would corrupt the cached loose-variable range.
a negative projection index raised Invalid_argument from List.nth, exiting with the runtime's own code 2.
an empty file was accepted: with no declarations there is nothing to accept, and no format was declared.
a file whose first line is not the meta line does not say which format version it is.
an exponent of a hundred million would build a number of that many bits: the result is refused (a decline), never computed and never guessed.
a base of a hundred bits to a five-million power overruns the size cap: the result is refused (a decline), never computed and never guessed.

Sort 4 is declared to have type (fun x => Sort 1) Prop, which reduces to Sort 1 while Sort 4 : Sort 5. A quick 'different sorts' verdict after reduction must stay a rejection (found by mutation testing: flipping it to 'equal' survived every test).
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type

files.why: an unsafe or partial constant is recorded with its type only, and no safe declaration can mention it.

Nat.add is redefined as fun a b => a, and the file claims Nat.add 123456789 987654321 = 1111111110 by rfl. With the shortcut keyed on the name the kernel would take the sum from GMP and accept; the fingerprint of the redefined constant is not the genuine one, so literals are unfolded through the file's own definition and the claim fails.
files.msg: the value does not have the declared type
